title: A lower third wears the mock's Lower-third badge on the canvas
goal: The captions mock shows a small Lower-third tag riding on the top edge of the violet plate while that style is picked, so you can tell at a glance the captions are a lower third. The app now puts the captions low left on the plate but shows no tag.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-captions.html .l3badge (line ~39, ~477): top:-11px left:0 of the plate, var(--comp) fill, 8.5px 640 weight, ic-component icon. The app plate hugs the words inside the Captions box (TextRasterizer.drawPlate), so the tag needs the plate rect, not the box. Chrome overlay like the AUTO · EN badge (CaptionGuides.swift CaptionBadge). Found by the-lower-third-caption-style-sits-low-left-on-i.
acceptance: On a video with captions in the Lower third style at Next defaults, a small Lower-third tag sits on the plate's top left edge in the editor, as video-captions.html draws it
The tag is never drawn into a frame written out, and is gone when another style is picked
If the tag's component icon promises something the app does not have (captions are not a component), a decision card asks the user before it ships

log.note: review before building: the tag is canvas chrome (like AUTO · EN), sized in screen points not picture points as the mock's 8.5px tag is, riding the plate's top left at -11px. It needs the plate's rect, which only the text rasterizer knows (plate hugs the words, not the box), so the rasterizer gets a public plateRect that shares drawPlate's union. Risk found: the app already draws a violet chip with the component glyph on the canvas for every component instance (CanvasComponents.swift, ComponentPaint violet). The mock's tag is that exact chip, so wearing the glyph would tell a person their captions are a component, which they are not. Building the tag with the label only and asking the user about the glyph on a card (acceptance 3). Premiere/FCP check: neither labels a caption style on the canvas; this is a chrome hint like the safe-area slabs, gone in the film.

the question "Should the Lower-third tag on the captions wear the mock's four-diamond icon?" was taken down without an answer: reopened with option d no longer retiring the task: the tag is already built, so no tag means removing it. Nobody chose anything, so nothing here was decided.

built: TextRasterizer.plateRect (shares drawPlate's union via plateBounds), LowerThirdTag in CaptionGuides.swift, EditorState.lowerThirdPlates, tag drawn in CaptionGuidesOverlay in the caption's own face at 8.5pt semibold on the fixed component violet. Walk lower-third-sits-low-left-walk gains captionsExpectLowerThirdTag / captionsExpectNoLowerThirdTag, ok at Next defaults with real captures; captions-panel-keeps-its-margins and captions-write-themselves walks ok. Exported frame at 4.31s checked: no tag. Icon held back for decision card. Left rough (not filed, agent-only): the walk 'render' step draws the untimed document, so with captions every cue stacks on one picture; use a frame from the exported film instead. Audit rough line 3 (tag follows the whole line's plate) stays here: the lower third look shows the whole line at once by default.

Tag shipped in d26ae25c: a violet Lower-third tag rides the top left of a lower third's plate in the editor, in the caption's face, never in the exported film, gone under other styles; lower-third-sits-low-left-walk checks it at Next defaults (ok, real captures), audit 2026-10-11-lower-third-tag.json. Waiting on the card about which icon the tag wears (the mock's component icon would read as a component chip); it shows the label only until answered.
decision "Which icon should the Lower-third tag on the captions wear?" resolved: Label only, as built now
Tag shipped in d26ae25c (audit 2026-10-11-lower-third-tag.json); the icon card was answered Label only, as built now, so nothing is left to build. Closed by the 2026-10-12 triage.
